# (PART) Fitting {-}

# Fitting overview

<!-- SCAFFOLD: signposting only. Eliot to expand with the statistical detail --
     which model form each sub-model uses, what the fitted objects contain, and
     how to judge whether a fit is usable. See #2. -->

Fitting is the first of the two stages in the fireSense workflow.
Each of the three processes the model represents -- ignition, escape and spread --
has its own statistical model, estimated from observed fire and covariate data
for the study area.

The chapters in this part follow the order a fitting workflow runs in.
`fireSense_dataPrepFit` assembles the covariates and the fire observations into
the form the fitting modules expect, so it runs first and the three fitting
modules draw on what it produces.
`fireSense_IgnitionFit`, `fireSense_EscapeFit` and `fireSense_SpreadFit` then
estimate their respective sub-models independently of one another.

The fitted objects these modules produce are the inputs to the prediction stage.
Nothing in this part simulates fire; that happens once the fitted models are
handed to the modules in [Predicting overview].
